questions: How many Cr chains did you assemble and measure at each length, and how many of the long chains showed zero-bias modes at both ends? Is the chain used for the RF data (written "Cr ∗ 12" on p. 4) the same chain as in Fig. 4?
Why were the other chains set aside, for example chains that ruptured or faulted from the strain you describe in S6, or chains without end modes?
Which lengths did you build and measure beyond Cr4, Cr5, Cr8 and Cr12 (Cr6, Cr7, Cr9 to Cr11, longer than 12), and did you take any spectra in magnetic field?
What does the second-best long chain, or a second Cr12, look like?

What is your energy resolution (30 µV lock-in excitation, effective electron temperature), and what upper bound on the end-mode splitting do the measured Cr12 end spectra set, next to the calculated 16.8 µeV?

Which Rashba coupling produced Figs. 2(b), 3, 4 and the 16.8 µeV splitting: the 1.8 eV·Å from DFT or the 3.6 eV·Å of S4? How do the splitting and ξM change between the two, given the measured 204 µeV gap against the calculated 84 and 146 µeV?
Could you perturb one end of a long chain (move or remove the end atom, or add a defect) and show whether the far end's mode stays at zero energy?
Which mass enters Eq. (1), and how does ξM shift if you keep cos(kF L) with kF L of about 19.4 rad? With a 4.75 Å spacing, 10.5 Å is about 2.2 sites; how did you arrive at three?
